The Mola di Veio waterfall is very characteristic, next to the ancient mill.
A lovely walk, comfortable clothing, plenty of water, and a camera are recommended.

Piordo stream waterfall.
Currently under a ban due to a landslide on the upper ridge.
Half an hour from Rome. Convenient and easy to reach by road. There's a parking lot. Great for dogs and children.

From lunchtime onwards the old abandoned structure begins to cast shade on the side where you can lie down, comfortable stone floor, the water comes from the basin above full of fish, some very large, I don't think the water is clean but the shower under the waterfalls is a must and I don't have gills or four ears yet so you survive
Nice, quiet without people, Etruscan park

The waterfall originates from a small dam built near the ancient Mola, a watermill built by the Orsini family in the 14th century and in operation until the 1950s. The cascade, approximately 18 meters high, creates a picturesque lake surrounded by centuries-old oak trees and lush vegetation.

We tried to do the loop, but because of the sheepdogs, we couldn't complete the last stretch. What a shame 😔
Otherwise, I highly recommend it; it's in the middle of the countryside... It's truly relaxing.
We started from the Isola Farnese cemetery, and after passing the waterfall, we continued following the signs. There are several forks along the route, so I recommend studying it carefully beforehand, but the elevation gain is almost non-existent (except for a small uphill section). Great fun!
Location, used in cinema.

It's easy to get to and has plenty of parking. A circular trail through the woods starts at the waterfall, but it's a shame that much of the trail is exposed to the sun and not in the woods near the river. So, plan your visit carefully, especially the time of day.

The waterfall takes its name from an ancient mill that used water power for grinding, likely in the Middle Ages or modern times (the old building next to the waterfall). The area is rich in historical layers: from prehistoric villages to medieval towns, including Roman villas and modern farmhouses.

Today, it is a landscape icon of the Veio Park, easily accessible from Formello or Isola Farnese, and appreciated for its double waterfall, the second of which reaches about 20 meters.
Beautiful, naturalistic place surrounded by greenery
Immersed in nature
Abandoned place. I'm sad because it could offer so much more to visitors.
Lovely place, absolutely worth seeing

A beautiful place to spend entire days practicing sports, with several marked trails for cycling, horseback riding, and trekking, or simply relaxing on the lawn near the river and breathing in the fresh air.

So much to discover.

An incredible place, absorbed by the city but still enduring thanks to its history and natural beauty. Etruscans, Romans, trails of the
Via Francigena, an ancient mill. Pristine wild fauna and flora. A picnic area suitable for long walks with your four-legged friend. Not to mention that the building that housed the ancient mill was used as the location for the famous tavern scene from the movie Pinocchio, when the cat and the fox invite Pinocchio to bury the
Coins. Various TV series. A historic place just steps from the city where you can unwind for a few hours.
Beautiful, I returned there after many years.

Very nice park, nice walk.

An interesting spot with the option of various walking trails through the greenery. Bring suitable footwear and, above all, water; there are no refill stations along the trails. A pleasant walk for nature lovers.
Beautiful, with trails starting from the waterfall. Parking nearby.
I was disappointed, the place is poorly maintained, many paths are closed and the open ones are unmarked so it's impossible to know where they lead.
